unknown_outcomes.rationale: A two-second fixture watchdog is not an API latency contract or production liveness proof.
Absent a verified pair of blocked sends, timeout alone is unknown rather than a detected cycle.
If no finite-drain or acknowledgement ordering receipt exists, do not infer which select case ran.
Host starvation after acknowledgement is not automatically an implementation deadlock.
A call blocked behind the same unfinished Once is not a second independent failure family.
A recorded Reset request does not prove real timer firing, and equality at twice respTimeout is outside this near precondition.
Both far matchers removed may describe a separately pinned cursor-fix candidate; it is not the outcome of the declared original source.
Synthetic far deadlines cannot establish wall-clock rollback reachability with monotonic timestamps.
A next-before-remove candidate can reach tail, but candidate identity and timer state must be recorded separately from original-source expectation.
Later outer-loop events may reset the timer; this bounded single invocation does not prove indefinite loss.
A response callback's ok and requestDone are different values; matching is not identical to completion. These branches remain one proposed mechanism family.
An exit return would require a readiness change inconsistent with the stipulated select; inspect actual trace before assigning a fault.
No deterministic outer-loop termination bound follows from source or a fixture's watchdog.
After closure return the outer select can process another ready event or exit; closure return alone does not prove worker leak or whole-function return.
Distinguish closure and goroutine/function return coordinates and counters.
Neither allowed branch is a product violation until cancellation linearization and accepted-work policy are independently defined.
Do not require a 50/50 frequency, priority for exit, or infer bug from a single ready-send choice.
Finite observation without return alone establishes neither unbounded starvation nor a leak; record window and events.
Multiple outer-loop iterations remain correlated traces, not independent shutdown defects.
Gossip nil and SendWBFTConsensus nil do not prove network delivery or consensus acceptance.
Missing broadcaster/targets/peers yields no attempt and is outside this ready-peer precondition, not automatic send failure.
Whether suppression after an error violates product retry policy requires independent best-effort/cache-contract review; no defect is asserted.
Other routes, cache eviction or expiration may enable later delivery; no permanent/global loss conclusion.
Parent nil is not the asynchronous sender result; ownership and result timestamps must remain separate.
A delayed fake sender is not observed network backpressure or a leak in a live deployment.
Global knownMessages insertion here is not used as the per-peer skip condition; distinct peer/hash policy must be evaluated locally.
Fresh cache does not imply independent family or prove eventual delivery.
If reorg has no adds or StateAt fails, the stipulated send was not reached; do not count an easy return as a valid normal trial.
Documented buffering/backpressure obligations may assign responsibility to caller; no operational defect or safety verdict.
This one-event control proves no claim about full buffers, multiple subscribers, repeated events or all-load safety.
Free capacity must be captured at Send, not assumed from channel capacity at construction.
Subscription removal is not the pool unlock itself and imposes no immediate end-to-end timing bound.
If another subscriber still blocks Send, lack of return does not refute removal of this subscriber.
